visuals.title: From leg to lung
visuals.text: Clot usually forms in a deep leg vein, travels through the right heart and lodges in the pulmonary arteries.

glossary.Embolism: Blockage of a blood vessel by material, such as a clot, that has travelled from elsewhere in the circulation.
glossary.Pulmonary arteries: Vessels carrying deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
glossary.Hypoxia: Too little oxygen reaching the tissues.
glossary.Hypoxaemia: Low oxygen level in arterial blood.
glossary.Cardiovascular collapse: Sudden failure of the circulation with very low blood pressure and loss of consciousness.
glossary.Thrombophilia: An inherited or acquired tendency for blood to clot too easily.
glossary.COCP: Combined oral contraceptive pill, containing oestrogen and progestogen; raises clotting risk.
glossary.HRT: Hormone replacement therapy, oestrogen given after menopause; raises clotting risk.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Hyperventilation: Breathing faster or deeper than needed, blowing off carbon dioxide.
glossary.Syncope: Brief loss of consciousness from reduced blood flow to the brain.
glossary.Hypotension: Low blood pressure, usually systolic below 90 mmHg.
glossary.Haematology: The medical specialty dealing with blood and clotting disorders.
glossary.Sensitivity: How well a test picks up people who have the disease; a negative highly sensitive test rules it out.
glossary.Specificity: How well a test is negative in people without the disease; a positive specific test rules it in.
glossary.Iodine allergy: Reaction to iodine-based contrast dye used in CT scans.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function over hours to days.
glossary.Compression duplex USS: Leg ultrasound that checks if veins squash and blood flows; a vein that will not compress contains clot.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Treatment that reduces blood clotting to stop clots growing or forming.
glossary.Proximal leg vein: Deep veins above the knee, such as the popliteal and femoral veins.
glossary.SpO2: Oxygen saturation measured by a pulse oximeter.
glossary.Outpatient: Treated at home without being admitted to hospital.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram: a recording of the heart's electrical activity.
glossary.Sinus tachycardia: Normal heart rhythm but faster than 100 beats per minute.
glossary.T wave inversion: Upside-down T wave on the ECG, a sign of ischaemia or strain.
glossary.Warfarin: Oral anticoagulant blocking vitamin K-dependent clotting factors; dose guided by INR.
glossary.Bridging: Covering with an injectable anticoagulant until warfarin takes full effect.
glossary.Recurrent VTE: A new clot after a previous one.
glossary.ABCDE: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure: the structured approach to an acutely unwell patient.
glossary.Non-rebreathe mask: Face mask with a reservoir bag that delivers high-concentration oxygen.
glossary.Shock: Inadequate blood flow to organs, causing tissue hypoxia.
glossary.Contraindication: A reason a treatment should not be given because the harm could outweigh the benefit.
glossary.CNS bleed: Bleeding inside the brain or spinal cord.
glossary.Haemorrhagic stroke: Stroke caused by bleeding into the brain.
glossary.Catheter intervention: Removing or breaking up a clot using a tube passed through the blood vessels.
glossary.Pulmonary vascular resistance: The resistance the lung circulation offers to blood pumped by the right ventricle.
glossary.Tricuspid regurgitation: Backflow of blood through the tricuspid valve into the right atrium.
glossary.Right heart failure: Failure of the right ventricle to pump blood forward, causing raised JVP and oedema.
glossary.Bronchoconstriction: Narrowing of the airways by contraction of their smooth muscle.
glossary.Vasoactive mediators: Chemicals released from the clot and platelets, such as serotonin, that narrow vessels and airways.
glossary.Venous stasis: Slow or stagnant blood flow in veins, e.g. during immobility.
glossary.Endothelial injury: Damage to the inner lining of a blood vessel, which triggers clotting.
glossary.Hypercoagulability: Blood that clots more readily than normal.
glossary.Ventricle: One of the two lower pumping chambers of the heart.
glossary.V1-V3: Chest ECG leads overlying the right ventricle and septum.
glossary.Immobilisation: Being unable to move about, e.g. bed rest or a leg in plaster.
